question: to the Commission Kathleen Funchion (The Left) Subject:

Various reports suggest that Irish infrastructure projects often run past deadlines and over budget. The Irish Fiscal Advisory Council last year also released figures to show that Irish productivity in the construction sector falls below the EU average. Many parts of Ireland are also over-reliant on roads for transport, and when necessary works are carried out on infrastructure bottlenecks, they can cause significant delays. Such delays result in massive disruption, particularly for people with disabilities, who find themselves cut off from vital services for the duration of the works. With this in mind has the commission monitored Ireland’s provision of adequate alternatives for people with disabilities under Directive 2024/2841? If so, what was the opinion of the Commission?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (29.9.2026) Transport is a policy area of shared competence between the EU and the Member States1. However, the primary responsibility for planning, financing, procuring and developing transport infrastructure lies with the Member States. Directive 2024/28412 is intended to ensure that persons with disabilities, when visiting or travelling to another Member State, can access the special conditions and preferential treatment available in the host country, on equal terms and conditions as its residents. By 5 June 2027, Member States shall adopt and publish the laws, regulations and administrative provisions necessary to comply with this Directive. They shall apply those measures from 5 June 2028. The EU and all its Member States, including Ireland, are parties to the United Nations Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (UNCRPD)3. In line with its Article 9, State Parties shall identify and eliminate obstacles and barriers to accessibility in, inter alia, the built environment, including buildings, roads, transportation and other indoor and outdoor facilities. Furthermore, in May 2026, the Commission adopted the Communication ‘Enhancing the Strategy for the rights of persons with disabilities’4, in which it put forward a Flagship initiative ‘Better access to transport for persons with disabilities’, covering various means of transport.
